2.note: Cross-reference to chapter 14 of Imrei Binah.

3.he: ראש חכמי הנוצרים ספר ט"ו פרק ט"ו מעירו
3.note: Augustine, De civitate Dei. The discussion of delayed procreation is in XV.15.

4.note: The sense of the comparison is uncertain. The sentence could mean that Maimonides' view (Guide II:47) is relevant here, rather than that it is preferable; seg. 65 then expresses reservation about it.

5.note: The phrase probably refers to the view that all the antediluvians were long-lived, which is the plain sense of the Torah; the reference is uncertain.

6.note: Pliny, Naturalis historia VII.2. The Hebrew name is transliterated because I cannot securely identify the authority Pliny cites at this point.

7.note: Pliny (NH VII.2) attributes the report about Indian women who give birth at five and die by eight chiefly to Megasthenes. Artemidorus is kept as the author gives him.

8.note: Solinus, Collectanea rerum memorabilium. The chapter number depends on the edition; the reference is kept as given.

9.he: בשביעי מספר ההנהגה המדינית פרק א'
9.note: The marriage ages appear in Politics VII.16 (37 and 18). The chapter number and the age 36 are kept as given.

10.note: The material seems closer to Historia animalium (e.g. VII.1) or De generatione animalium than to book IV. The reference is kept as given.

11.note: Identified as Jean Fernel (Fernelius), Universa medicina, whose second part is the Pathologia.

12.note: An allusion to Isaiah's sign-children (Isa 7–8). The construction of the sentence is uncertain.
